used_notes: Yes, decisively and in both directions: the notes reversed my statistics-only call on roughly a dozen candidates, because for most candidates the note count equals total_reports (so the notes are the complete evidence), and in cases like C-8, C-6, C-41, C-17, C-35, C-10, C-51, C-15 and C-42 a textbook-looking ordered 4-5 link chain turned out to have no note that names the candidate entity at all (the events belong to neighbouring entities such as basalt-pay or wisteria-edge), while C-26's three-link chain that looks cross-regional in the aggregates is in the notes reported entirely from one site (R01S00) with total_reports triple independent_sources, i.e. one loud site echoing itself; conversely the notes rescued C-11, whose component_defect first_seen_day of d3 is an unrelated inventory note (the real tundrax defect reports start d12, after the d8 supplier substitution), and C-14, whose policy_change/manual_workaround tie at day 19 resolves to 19 then 29 once the org-tagged notes are read.
reasoning_notes:
Method: for each candidate I mapped its links onto the seven causal chains, checked (a) how many links lie on ONE chain, (b) whether first_seen_day is monotonically increasing along that chain's order, (c) whether each link has >=2 independent sources, and (d) in the raw notes, whether the events are actually attributed to the candidate entity and whether the reporting org paths (REGION-SITE-DEPT-TEAM-USER) for different links come from different parts of the org rather than one site repeating itself.

Top tier (put in front of an executive): C-12 nimbusx532 walks the whole cert_rotation->auth_failure->api_error_spike->checkout_drop->revenue_miss chain (d52/60/70/97/120) with each stage reported from a different region (R01, R00S02, R04, R06, R01). C-28 kestrel-pay covers all six links of the supply chain in order with 10 independent defect reports spanning R06/R04/R01 and escalations from R03/R05/R04. C-30 meridian-pay is the second clean full B-chain. C-9 peregrine-edge runs manual_workaround->data_exposure_risk->audit_finding->regulatory_notice with each stage a burst from a different site (R01S00, R04S01, R05S00, R06). C-47 basalt and C-39 zephyr-core495 are full attrition->backlog->sla->penalty->churn progressions; C-7 arbor-apac is a tight, tightly ordered four-link version of the same chain, entity-named in almost every note. C-56 tundra-core and C-53 arbor-pay are clean full price_increase->margin_compression->discount_escalation->forecast_revision chains with a different region behind each stage. C-45 nimbus-pay (compliance chain), C-11 tundrax, C-38 meridian, C-46 halcyon-pay (supply chain), C-29 lumen (network/close chain), C-31 pellucid (firmware/sensor/downtime), C-59 zephyr-na and C-14 arbor-hub round out the list.

Deliberate exclusions despite strong-looking statistics: C-20 thistle (7-8 sources per link but component_defect d0, escalation d2, substitution d3, revenue_miss d7 - no causal progression at all, just a high-traffic entity); C-24 solace (forecast_revision d21 precedes discount_escalation d22 precedes margin_compression d25 - exactly reversed against chain F); C-26 halcyon-net (single loud site, echo-inflated totals); C-34 peregrine (regulatory_notice starts d21, before the exposure/audit it should follow, and two of its policy notes are near-duplicate text from the same dept); C-16, C-5, C-32, C-49, C-54 (links out of causal order); C-35, C-22, C-18, C-19, C-44 (chains resting on single reports); and the large group whose notes never mention the entity.

Borderline kept out: C-37 (nimbusx532 on the people/SLA chain - good spread but contract_penalty d49 precedes sla_breach d50), C-0, C-1 (data_exposure_risk d29 precedes its policy_change), C-58 (regulatory_notice unsupported in notes; audit_finding duplicated from one user id), C-48 and C-55 (only one link actually entity-attributed in the notes).
